item.title: [stayInformed] Limits in Copilot Chat
item.description:
Microsoft uses fair use limits for some Copilot features for users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

Features, such as image generation, already use limits, as previously communicated in MC1064749. We are applying this approach to additional Copilot Chat features and capabilities.

Users will be notified in-product if the capacity or feature is not available.

Rollout Schedule

Limits are currently used for some Copilot Chat capabilities and may expand to additional capabilities over time. New Copilot Chat limits are currently rolling out.

Impact on Your Organization

Who is affected:

Users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license in commercial tenants.

Platforms/Services:

 When using Copilot Chat in apps (web, desktop, and mobile).

What will happen:

  • Fair use provides users with access to a feature with limits and can vary throughout the day.
  • For either type of limit, the user can try the feature or capability again later. Microsoft will be clear on the timeframe in product.
  • Responses already in progress will not be interrupted.
  • Microsoft sets and manages these limits. Admins can't view or adjust the limits.

Action Required/Recommendations

No action is required.

We recommend that admins:

  • Inform help desk staff that some Copilot Chat capabilities will be limited for users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • Review Limits for features and capabilities in Microsoft Copilot Chat | Microsoft Support for more information about how access may vary.
  • Review Manage self-service license requests in the Microsoft 365 admin center to understand how your organization can manage self-service license requests.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Office in Copilot brings the full power of Office into the Microsoft Copilot app
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Now users have the full power of Office in Microsoft Copilot app, so users can create, edit and collaborate on Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, without leaving the app.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 and expect to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Now with the full value of Office in Copilot,  Word, Excel, and PowerPoint is brought in directly into the Copilot experience, allowing users to create, review, edit, and collaborate on Office files without leaving their flow of work. This reduces context switching and makes it easier to move from an idea or conversation to a finished, shareable Office artifact.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required. Admins may want to inform users about the new experience and review their existing Microsoft 365 Copilot configuration and policies.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Users can now access and edit Office file content through the Copilot experience, with changes synced back to the regular Office apps.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Copilot gains expanded capability to read and edit Office document content as part of this feature.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can create and edit Word, Excel, and PowerPoint content directly within the Copilot app.
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. This feature is subject to existing Microsoft 365 Copilot configuration and policies, which admins can manage via Entra ID group-based assignment.

item.title: [stayInformed] Power Platform - Newer GPT models replace Anthropic, Grok, and earlier GPT models
item.description:
We are updating the models available in prompts in Copilot Studio, Power Automate and Power Apps to bring newer OpenAI GPT models to the Basic, Standard, and Premium tiers, with no change to tier pricing. As part of this update, we’re retiring the Anthropic and Grok models and earlier GPT models listed below. Existing prompts using these models will automatically move to the replacement for their current tier, providing access to newer models while preserving your tier selection. This update will be applied on December 2, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This change affects makers, administrators, and users of solutions that use prompts configured with one of the retiring models, including prompts used in Power Apps, Power Automate, and Microsoft Copilot Studio. The models listed below will be fully retired by December 2, 2026. Automatic migration of affected prompts will be completed by this date.

Tier Retiring model Replacement model
Basic GPT-4.1 mini GPT-6 Luna
Standard GPT-4.1, GPT-5 chat, GPT-5.3 chat, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Grok 4.1 Fast reasoning ChatGPT-latest
Premium GPT-5 reasoning, GPT-5.2 reasoning, Claude Opus 4.6 GPT-6 Reasoning
  • Migration is automatic for affected prompts. Makers do not need to select a replacement to receive the update.
  • Tier pricing will not change as part of this migration. Actual consumption and costs can vary with usage, including input and output token counts.
  • Responses can differ after migration, including wording, formatting, and how instructions are followed. Review solutions that depend on specific output structures or behavior.
  • After retirement, the previous models will no longer be available in prompts. Keeping an affected prompt configured with a retiring model will not prevent migration.
What action do I need to take?
Review and test your affected prompts before December 2, 2026. To do this:
  1. Identify prompts using the retiring models and the apps, flows, and agents that depend on them.
  2. Test with the replacement model for each tier as it becomes available in the prompt builder. Use representative inputs to check response quality, output formats, and downstream processing.
  3. Adjust prompt instructions or dependent workflows where testing identifies differences.
  4. Notify affected makers and support teams and monitor prompt results and consumption after migration.
Please note that no action is required to trigger automatic migration.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Suggestions to continue in another Copilot experience
item.description:
[What and why]

The Chat experience in the Copilot app will suggest a better-fit mode based on the user's prompt, if applicable. For example, it will suggest Cowork or other supported modes as they become available. Users will see a suggestion card after they send a prompt in Chat, with an explanation of the better-fit mode and an option for the user to switch to the suggested mode. Their chat conversation will be attached to the prompt in the new mode to maintain context. Only users who have the Copilot mode (example Cowork) enabled will see this experience.

[Rollout schedule]

  •  General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who have access to supported Copilot modes, such as Cowork.

Platforms and services

  •  Microsoft Copilot

What will happen

  • After sending a prompt in Chat, if Copilot determines that another Copilot experience available to the user may better fit a request or task, the user may see a banner suggesting that experience.
  • In the banner, the user will see an option to switch to the suggested experience (ie. Cowork) or remain in Chat. 
  • If the user selects the option to switch, they will be brought directly to the suggested experience with the prompt already sent, along with the context from their Chat conversation attached.
  • Users will see suggestions only for experiences they can access. For example, users who do not have access to Cowork will not see a suggestion to use Cowork.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required to prepare for this change.

Consider informing your users and help desk that Copilot may suggest another Copilot mode when that mode may better fit a request or task.

Consider reviewing which users are included in a spending policy that grants Cowork access, and confirm your intended usage-based billing configuration. 

[Compliance considerations]

 No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Changes to Word, Excel, and PowerPoint agents in Microsoft Copilot
item.description:
What and why

We are replacing the standalone Word, Excel, and PowerPoint agents with document-creation and editing capabilities built into the Copilot app for users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL). In Copilot Chat, users can ask Copilot to create or refine a document, workbook, or presentation directly. Copilot will use its integrated capabilities rather than invoke the standalone agents.

Rollout schedule

Worldwide General Availability rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.

Impact on your organization

This update affects all users with a USL who currently have access to the standalone Word, Excel, and PowerPoint agents.

In Chat, users can ask Copilot directly to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations, without selecting a standalone agent.

  • As the change reaches users, the standalone agents will be removed from the left rail and agent discovery. Users will no longer be able to find, pin, @mention, or invoke them as separate agents.
  • Previously generated files will remain in their existing OneDrive or SharePoint locations, subject to existing permissions and retention settings.
  • Previous conversation history will remain available to view. Users will not be able to continue working with the standalone agents in those conversations. To create documents or make edits, users should start a new conversation in Chat.

Action required / recommendations

No admin configuration or user setup is required. Inform affected users and helpdesk staff to start new document-creation and editing tasks directly in Chat, and update guidance that points users to the standalone agents.

Compliance considerations

This update introduces no changes to data processing. Existing file permissions and retention settings continue to apply. Changes to standalone-agent availability and conversation continuation are described above.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Conversation orchestration expands routing and overflow capabilities
item.description:
[What and why]

Conversation orchestration in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Contact center actively manages conversations throughout their lifecycle, from initiation through resolution. As conditions change, such as increasing wait times, queues filling quickly, or representatives going offline, conversation orchestration can automatically take actions defined in natural-language playbooks configured by administrators.

Administrators can configure playbooks for specific scenarios using guided templates. Built-in validation identifies conflicts before playbooks are published. These capabilities help organizations automate contact center processes while improving routing, continuity, and responsiveness.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using or planning to use Conversation Orchestration in Dynamics 365 Contact center

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Contact center 
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium)

What will happen

  • Dynamic priority escalation: Conversation priority can be reevaluated as a conversation progresses based on conditions such as wait-time thresholds, queue transfers, customer tier, or other context.
  • Overflow handling across multiple conditions: Administrators can configure actions for conditions such as queues being outside operating hours, representatives being signed out or unavailable, queue wait times exceeding a threshold, or the number of waiting conversations exceeding a specified limit. Actions can include offering callbacks, routing to alternate queues, expanding assignment eligibility, notifying supervisors, or providing contextual customer messages. Overflow handling can also be configured for direct inward dial calls when representatives are unavailable or do not accept calls.
  • Assignment to a previously engaged or preferred representative: Conversation orchestration can reconnect customers with previously engaged or preferred representatives based on factors including previous interactions, queue membership, availability, and workload capacity. For asynchronous conversations, organizations can choose to consider representative presence status and active conversation limits before reconnecting customers. If that representative is unavailable, the conversation can fall back to the next qualified representative.
  • Bullseye routing: Administrators can progressively expand the pool of eligible representatives when a conversation is not assigned within a defined timeframe. Routing rings can use skills, proficiency levels, teams, or other business criteria.
  • Existing customers using Conversation Orchestration can continue using their existing configurations without additional action.
  • New customers can enable Conversation Orchestration and configure playbooks.
  • Copilot credits are consumed when administrators publish playbooks. The feature does not consume Copilot credits during runtime execution.

Screenshot 2 - Conversation orchestration - Escalate priority view: 

[Action required and recommendations]

No additional preparation is required for existing customers.

For new customers:

  • Review the prerequisites for Conversation Orchestration.
  • Enable Conversation Orchestration.
  • Configure playbooks appropriate for your organization.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Increasing user exception limit to 10,000 for Standard-Deferred release preferences
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We heard your feedback that the 100-user exception limit was too small to support meaningful pilot and validation audiences, particularly in larger organizations. We previously introduced Microsoft Entra ID group support to simplify audience management. We are now increasing the exception limit from 100 to 10,000 users per tenant, giving administrators more flexibility to manage release readiness at scale.

This update lets you assign a larger audience to a release preference different from your tenant-wide selection - for example, keeping a larger validation group on Standard release while the rest of your organization uses Deferred release.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected: Administrators managing Standard and Deferred release preferences in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

What is changing:

  • The maximum exception audience increases to 10,000 users per tenant, counting users assigned individually and members of assigned groups together. This is not a per-group allowance or a limit on your organization total users.
  • You can continue using Microsoft Entra ID security groups to manage exceptions. Nested groups remain unsupported.
  • If your tenant uses Deferred release, you can assign a larger group of IT staff, help desk personnel, and business representatives to Standard release to evaluate eligible updates earlier.
  • If your tenant uses Standard release, you can assign a larger audience to Deferred release when those users need additional preparation time.
  • If a customer adds a group with more than 10,000 users, they will receive a message, during addition, notifying them of the limit.
  • If they add a group that later exceeds the limit, only the first 10,000 users will be included. The Release preferences in MAC will display a message asking them to remove the users who exceed the limit.

What is not changing: This update increases audience capacity; it does not change which features are eligible for Deferred release or how the deferred period works. Deferred release continues to delay eligible major features by approximately 30 days after their rollout to Standard release begins, not after rollout completes or after an individual pilot user receives the feature.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required unless you want to expand your exception audience.

Once the increased limit is available in your tenant, review your pilot and validation needs and update your assignments in the Microsoft 365 admin center under: Copilot > Settings > View all > Copilot Release Preferences: General Availability.

Keep the combined exception audience within 10,000 users, review group membership regularly, and update your internal rollout and readiness documentation as needed.

[Compliance considerations:]

When expanding your exception audience, review its membership against your organization change-management, validation, and governance requirements.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Facilitator Protection skill helps identify suspected social-engineering attempts
item.description:
[What and why]

Facilitator can help users identify suspected social-engineering attempts by people outside their organization during a meeting. When Facilitator is present, its Protection skill uses AI to check the meeting transcript for signs that someone may be attempting to trick users into sharing sensitive information. If a suspected attempt is detected, users will see a warning with options to end the meeting or temporarily restrict information sharing.

This feature can help organizations reduce the risk of sensitive information being disclosed through social engineering during meetings with external participants.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late January 2027 and expected to complete by mid-February 2027

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who use Facilitator in meetings with participants outside their organization

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Facilitator

What will happen

  • When Facilitator is present in a meeting with participants outside your organization, the Protection skill is invoked automatically.
  • The Protection skill uses AI to check the meeting transcript for signs of suspected social-engineering attempts.
  • If a suspected attempt is detected, users will receive a warning.
  • Users will have options to end the meeting or temporarily restrict information sharing.
  • No action is required to enable the Protection skill.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required to enable the Protection skill.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform users that they may receive warnings about suspected social-engineering attempts during meetings with external participants.
  • Help users understand the available options if a warning appears.
  • Review the Facilitator documentation to familiarize yourself with the feature.

[Compliance considerations]

This change introduces an AI capability that interacts with customer data. When Facilitator is present, the Protection skill uses AI to check the meeting transcript for signs of suspected social-engineering attempts.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: New accounting capabilities in Excel and Cowork
item.description:
[What and why]

New accounting capabilities in Copilot in Excel and Cowork help finance professionals complete common accounting tasks in the tools they already use. Users can reconcile accounts, prepare journal entries, analyze financial performance and variances, and prepare financial reports. Additional capabilities support budgeting, forecasting, audit, tax, compliance, and training.

Copilot prepares the work while users retain control of review, approval, and posting. Nothing is posted automatically to an ERP or system of record without approval.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview: We will begin rolling out in late October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-November 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on November 13, 2026, and expect to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Accountants, AP/AR specialists, controllers, and other finance professionals with a Microsoft Copilot licenses

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Copilot
  • Microsoft Excel
  • Cowork

What will happen

  • Users can reconcile accounts by comparing balances and transactions, identifying discrepancies, and preparing reconciling items for review.
  • Users can draft journal entries, including accruals, reclassifications, allocations, reversals, and recurring entries, with checks for required inputs and balanced entries.
  • Users can analyze financial performance against plan, identify key drivers, and prepare financial reporting and variance analysis.
  • Additional capabilities support budgeting, forecasting, audit, tax, compliance, and training.
  • In Excel and Cowork, finance professionals can choose to capture an audit trail when they invoke an accounting capability. When selected, a record of what Copilot changed and why is created in their chat history. Audit trails are currently available in Excel and are planned for Cowork.
  • Copilot works only with content each user can access, respects existing permissions and sensitivity labels, and stays within the Microsoft 365 service boundary.
  • Nothing is posted automatically to an ERP or system of record without user approval.
  • Accounting capabilities can use connectors as separate sources, including sources used to read from or write to ERP systems. The accounting capabilities do not depend on these connectors. Third-party accounting connectors may require separate licensing or admin enablement.

[Action required and recommendations]

Action required: During Public Preview, accounting capabilities in Excel and Cowork are available to users who have a Microsoft Copilot license and are enrolled in Microsoft Copilot Frontier. Beginning with General Availability on November 13, 2026, Frontier enrollment will not be required.

To provide access during Public Preview:

  • Assign Microsoft Copilot licenses to finance users who need access.
  • In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Settings > Frontier, turn on Frontier, and choose whether to provide access to all eligible users or specific users or groups, such as your finance team.
  • Enroll your admin account in Frontier if you need to see and manage Frontier features such as Cowork in the admin center.
  • Consider notifying your finance teams about the new accounting capabilities.

Learn more

  • Available plugins for Copilot Cowork | Microsoft Learn
  • Microsoft Copilot for finance: Purpose-built for the way finance teams work | Microsoft Copilot Blog
  • Use built-in skills and skills created by Microsoft with Copilot in Excel | Microsoft Support
  • Explore AI Early Access in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Frontier
  • Get Started with Frontier for IT Admins | Microsoft Frontier

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. The new accounting capabilities use Microsoft Copilot to perform accounting-related work using content the user can access.
Does the change provide end users a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Finance users can use Copilot accounting capabilities in Excel and Cowork for reconciliation, journal entries, analysis, and reporting.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Entra ID: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication to retire for self-service password reset (SSPR)
item.description:
[What and why]

As Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retire in Microsoft Entra ID, these methods will also become unavailable for SSPR. Organizations have 50 days after the applicable sign-in retirement rollout reaches their tenant to prepare alternative recovery methods. Users may still be able to sign in but lose the ability to reset forgotten passwords. Passkeys and other sign-in methods don't automatically satisfy SSPR requirements. Admins should identify affected users and ensure they have enough eligible recovery methods to prevent disruptions and increased helpdesk requests.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We expect rollout to begin and complete in February 2027

User populationSign-in retirement rollout beginsSSPR transition ends
Users other than Global Administrators and external usersFebruary 1, 202750 days after this rollout reaches your tenant
Global Administrators and external usersJuly 1, 202750 days after this separate rollout reaches your tenant

These are phased rollout start dates, not a single SSPR cutoff for every organization. Each population's 50-day period begins when its applicable rollout reaches your tenant. 

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations with users who rely on Microsoft-provided SMS/voice to meet their password-reset verification requirements. This includes users who have another sign-in method but still depend on SMS/voice for password recovery.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID SSPR

What will happen

When the applicable sign-in retirement rollout reaches your tenant:

  • 50-day transition: Existing SMS and voice registrations remain usable for SSPR under your current recovery policy.
  • Registration changes: SMS/voice SSPR registration and refresh prompts stop, but prompts for other eligible methods continue.
  • My Sign-Ins: Users can no longer add SMS/voice methods or edit authentication phone numbers. Existing phone registrations appear disabled, even while usable for SSPR during the transition.
  • Customer-managed telephony (CYOT): Recovery through supported providers remains available.

After the 50-day transition period:

Microsoft-provided SMS and voice are no longer available as SSPR recovery options.

User's remaining eligible recovery methodsPassword-reset experience
Enough methods to meet the applicable SSPR requirementUser can continue resetting their password with those methods
Not enough methods to meet the applicable SSPR requirementUser cannot complete SSPR and is directed to contact their administrator

The applicable one/two method requirement still applies. To retain SMS/voice for recovery, your organization must configure a supported CYOT.

Microsoft will not automatically change your SSPR policy or enable Allow password change after secure sign-in for your tenant.

[Action required and recommendations]

Prepare affected users before their applicable 50-day transition period ends:

  1. Identify affected users. Find users relying on SMS/voice for SSPR, even if they have other sign-in methods registered. Use the SMS and voice retirement and migration guidance.
  2. Prepare alternative recovery methods. Ensure users have enough eligible methods to meet SSPR policy requirements without Microsoft-provided SMS/voice. Passkeys alone don't satisfy SSPR requirements. If phone recovery is needed, configure and test a supported telephony provider before the transition ends.
  3. Test and communicate. Verify password recovery works with your SSPR policies and Conditional Access settings. Inform users and helpdesk staff about deadlines, registration steps, and support options.

Recommended: Let passkey users change a forgotten password

  • Where available, administrators can enable Allow password change after secure sign-in for eligible users. Users can then sign in with their passkey and change their password in My Sign-Ins without knowing/entering their current password.

Learn more

  • SMS and voice retirement and migration guidance
  • How Microsoft Entra self-service password reset works
  • Choose a telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication

[Compliance considerations]

If your organization needs phone-based recovery for regulatory or operational reasons, plan and validate a supported customer-managed provider before the applicable SSPR cutoff.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Viva Engage: Flexible targeting of Storyline Announcements
item.description:
Updated November 2, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

We’re introducing My Team audiences and expanded targeting capabilities in Viva Engage to help leaders communicate with the employees in their organization and tailor messages to relevant teams, departments, locations, or groups. My Team provides a ready-to-use, automatically maintained audience based on the organizational hierarchy, so leaders can reach the employees who report up to them, including both direct and indirect reports. This audience helps unlock and improve leadership experiences across Viva Engage, making Storyline Announcements, audience analytics, Leadership Corner, and feed and digest distribution more relevant with less setup.

Leaders and delegates can use My Team as-is, review its membership, or further customize and save it as a reusable audience across leader communication experiences. For Storyline Announcements, they can also define recipients at the time of publish, choosing My Team, a saved audience, or a custom audience built using organizational attributes such as department, job title, or country; existing groups like M365 Groups, distribution lists, or security groups; and individual users by name. Together, My Team and flexible targeting make leader communications more relevant, scalable, and easier to manage - with a dynamic default audience and precise targeting for relevant employee groups.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 499895.

[When this will happen:]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Begins mid-November 2025 and completes by mid-March 2026 (previously early February).
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Begins mid-January 2027 (previously early November 2026) and completes by late February 2027 (previously late November 2026).

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected: Leaders and delegates using Viva Engage Storyline Announcements in tenants enrolled in public preview.

What will happen:

  • This capability is being introduced as part of the public preview for Viva Engage. During this phase, leaders and their delegates can actively experiment with flexible audience targeting for Storyline Announcements—defining a custom audience at the time of posting, rather than relying solely on pre‑configured Leader Audiences.
  • Audiences can include organizational attributes (such as reporting structure, country, department, job title), existing groups (Microsoft 365 Groups, DLs, SGs), or individual users.
  • Notifications and delivery channels (Teams, email, Viva Engage Inbox) remain unchanged for recipients.
  • No dependency on IT or advance audience setup—leaders can act immediately when communication needs arise.
  • Available only in public preview; functionality and targeting options may evolve before general availability.
  • Admins should ensure organizational attributes in Entra ID or Organizational Data in Microsoft are accurate to support successful targeting.
  • Available platforms: Desktop and web.
  • Licensing requirements: This feature requires a premium license available through Viva or Communications and Communities (C&C). Availability may vary depending on your organization's Microsoft 365 licensing agreement.

[What you can do to prepare:]

No admin action is required for rollout. To prepare, you may want to:

  • Validate organizational attributes (reporting structure, country, department, role, job title) in Microsoft Entra ID or Organizational Data in Microsoft.
  • Confirm leader and delegate assignments to ensure the right people can use Storyline Announcements and the new targeting control.

Learn more:

  • Use your organizational data in Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Viva | Microsoft Viva | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Breakout room support for Teams Rooms on Android
item.description:

This feature improves coordination during breakout sessions and brings Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android closer to feature parity with Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows. This enhancement is based on customer feedback and helps organizations deliver a more consistent meeting experience across Teams Rooms devices.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early December 2026 (previously mid-November) and expected to be complete by mid-December 2026 (previously late November)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android devices
  • Meeting organizers who use breakout rooms in Microsoft Teams meetings

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) General Availability: Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows
item.description:
Updated October 30, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[Introduction]

Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows will soon be Generally Available, enabling phishing‑resistant, passwordless sign‑in to Microsoft Entra‑protected resources from Windows devices.

The Public Preview of this capability was previously announced in MC1247893.

Users can create device‑bound passkeys stored in the Windows Hello container and authenticate using Windows Hello methods (face, fingerprint, or PIN). This expands passwordless authentication support to Windows devices that aren’t Microsoft Entra‑joined or registered, helping organizations strengthen security and reduce reliance on passwords across corporate‑managed, personal, and shared device scenarios.

[When this will happen:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out in late April 2026 and expect to complete by mid‑June 2026.
  • General Availability (GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out in early February 2027 (previously early October 2026) and expect to complete by late February 2027 (previously late October 2026)
  • For Airgap: We will begin rolling out in early May 2027 and expect to complete by late May 2027.

How this affects your organization:

Who is affected:

Organizations using Microsoft Entra ID with passkeys enabled in the Authentication Methods policy whose users sign in from Windows devices, including:

  • Corporate‑managed PCs
  • Personal devices
  • Shared devices

What will happen:

With this General Availability release:

  • Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows will no longer require explicit opt‑in through Windows Hello AAGUID allow‑listing in a passkey (FIDO2) profile.
  • This represents a change from Public Preview behavior, where administrators were required to explicitly allow Windows Hello AAGUIDs in a passkey profile for Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows to function.
  • If your passkey profile allows device‑bound, non‑attested passkeys:
    • Users scoped to that profile will now be able to register and use Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows by default without additional administrator configuration.
  • As a result:
    • Users in scope of passkey profiles that allow device‑bound, non‑attested passkeys may begin registering and using passkeys on Windows devices.
    • If Conditional Access policies allow:
      • Passkeys can be created and used on Windows devices that are not Microsoft Entra‑joined or registered, including personal or shared PCs.
  • Each Windows device requires separate passkey registration per Entra account.
  • Windows Hello for Business remains recommended for managed, Microsoft Entra‑joined or registered devices.
  • Passkeys on Windows supplement unmanaged or shared device scenarios and do not support device sign‑in.
  • Attestation is not currently supported for Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows but is planned for a future update.

What you can do to prepare:

No action is required for most organizations.

If you do not want users to register or use Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows:

  • Update the relevant passkey (FIDO2) profile to block Windows Hello AAGUIDs.
  • Review existing passkey profiles that allow device‑bound, non‑attested passkeys.
  • Add Windows Hello AAGUIDs to the block list in passkey profiles where passkey usage on Windows devices should not be permitted.

Learn more: Enable Microsoft Entra passkey on Windows | Microsoft Learn (will be updated before GA rollout)

[Compliance considerations:]

Compliance areaExplanation
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable Conditional Access policies?Existing Conditional Access policies continue to govern whether passkeys can be created or used on unmanaged Windows devices.
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Admins can control passkey availability through Authentication Methods policies and FIDO2 passkey profiles scoped to Microsoft Entra ID groups.
Does the change allow a user to enable and disable the feature themselves?Users may register Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows devices if permitted by administrator policy configuration.

item.title: [planForChange] (Update)Microsoft Entra ID: General Availability of passkey profiles and migration for existing Passkeys (FIDO2) tenants
item.description:
Updated October 30, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[Introduction]

Starting in March 2026, Microsoft Entra ID will introduce passkey profiles and synced passkeys to General Availability (GA). This update allows administrators to opt in to a new passkey profiles experience that supports group-based passkey configurations and introduces a new passkeyType property.

Important: Only tenants that already have Passkeys (FIDO2) enabled are affected by this update.

The passkeyType property enables admins to configure:

  • Device-bound passkeys
  • Synced passkeys
  • Both

If your tenant already has Passkeys (FIDO2) enabled and you do not opt in to passkey profiles during the initial rollout window, your tenant will be automatically migrated to the passkey profiles schema at the date range specified below. When this occurs:

  • Existing Passkey (FIDO2) authentication method configurations will be moved into a Default passkey profile.
  • The passkeyType value will be set based on the tenant’s current attestation settings. Synced passkeys will be enabled for tenants with attestation enforcement disabled.
  • No new authentication methods are enabled as part of this migration.
  • This migration also impacts Authentication methods registration campaign set to “Microsoft managed” state, which uses passkey configuration settings to determine which registration prompts are shown to users.

Authentication Methods Registration Campaign changes (Microsoft-Managed Only)

Tenants are impacted when all the following conditions are met:

  • The Passkeys (FIDO2) authentication method policy is Enabled
  • Authentication methods registration campaign is set to “Microsoft managed” state
  • Allow self-service setup is Enabled
  • Target specific AAGUIDs is not selected (no AAGUID restrictions configured)
  • The Authentication Methods Registration Campaign state is set to Microsoft-managed
  • The tenant has at least one user enabled for both synced passkeys and device‑bound passkeys
    • Only users who are enabled for both synced passkeys and device‑bound passkeys, with no passkey profile restrictions configured (i.e. attestation enforcement, AAGUID restrictions), will receive a passkey registration nudge during sign‑in.

For these tenants, Microsoft-managed registration campaign settings will be updated after passkey profile automatic migration is complete. We will roll out changes incrementally to in-scope tenants according to the timeline outlined below.

[When this will happen]

Passkey profile and Synced passkeys General Availability

  • Public cloud Worldwide, GCC: Rollout begins in early March 2026 and is expected to complete by late March 2026
  • GCC High, DoD clouds: Rollout begins in early May 2026 and is expected to complete by late May 2026
  • USNat, USSec: Rollout begins in early April 2027 (previously early October 2026) and is expected to complete by late April 2027 (previously late October 2026)

Automatic migration for existing passkeys (FIDO2) enabled tenants

  • Public cloud Worldwide, GCC: Rollout begins in early May 2026 and is expected to complete by late June 2026
  • GCC High, DoD clouds: Rollout begins in early February 2027 (previously early October 2026) and is expected to complete by late February 2027 (previously late October 2026)
  • USNat, USSec: Rollout begins in early May 2027 (previously early October 2026) and is expected to complete by late May 2027 (previously late October 2026)

Authentication Methods registration campaign changes in Microsoft-Managed state (for in-scope tenants):

  • Public cloud Worldwide, GCC: Rollout begins in early May 2026 and is expected to complete by late June 2026

[How this affects your organization]

Automatic migration for existing passkeys (FIDO2) enabled tenants 

What will happen:

If you have not opted in to passkey profiles by your automatic enablement period, your tenant will be migrated to passkey profiles.

  • Your existing Passkey (FIDO2) configurations will be migrated into a Default passkey profile
  • New passkeyType property will be auto-populated
    • If enforce attestation is enabled, then device-bound allowed
    • If enforce attestation is disabled, then device-bound and synced allowed
  • Any existing key restrictions will remain intact
  • Any existing user targets will be assigned to the Default passkey profile

Authentication Methods registration campaign changes in Microsoft-Managed state (for in-scope tenants) 

What will happen:

Microsoft-managed registration campaign settings will be updated:

  • "Targeted authentication method” will change from Microsoft Authenticator to “passkeys (FIDO2)”.
  • “Days allowed to snooze” setting will change from 3days to “1 day”. This setting will no longer be configurable.
  • “Limited number of snoozes” setting will change from Enabled to "Disabled”. This setting will no longer be configurable.
  • The default user targeting will be updated from voice call or text message users to all multifactor authentication (MFA) capable users.

What is the end user impact:

Once the above changes have taken effect, users targeted in the registration campaign will begin to receive passkey registration nudges during sign-in flows after they have completed multifactor authentication.

[What you can do to prepare]

If you want a configuration different from the migration defaults, review the timeline above and opt in to passkey profiles before your tenant’s automatic enablement window begins. Then configure the Default passkey profile’s passkeyType to your preferred values.

We also recommend:

  • Review your registration campaign configuration, especially if its set to Microsoft-managed. If you do not want registration campaign to target passkeys, you can:
    • Switch the registration campaign state to Enabled and continue targeting Microsoft Authenticator, or
    • Set the registration campaign state to Disabled.
  • Update runbooks and help content so your help desk and end users understand any changes in passkey availability or behavior.

Learn more:

  • Enable passkeys for your organization - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • How to Enable Passkey (FIDO2) Profiles in Microsoft Entra ID (preview) - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • How to Enable Synced Passkeys (FIDO2) in Microsoft Entra ID (preview) - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Enhanced Copilot and AI controls for meetings
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft Teams is updating how administrators and meeting organizers configure AI for Teams meetings. The existing Copilot meeting policy is being replaced by two more specific policies:

  • MeetingAI - controls whether Copilot, Facilitator, Intelligent Recap, and other AI features are available in meetings.
  • TranscriptionWithMeetingAI - controls whether transcription starts automatically when meeting AI is turned on.

This gives administrators clearer, more predictable control over whether AI is available and whether it requires (or works without) transcription, including the ability to enforce Copilot off. Organizers also gain more visibility into, and in some cases control over, these settings directly from the meeting options.

Meeting options are also being updated to make AI controls easier to understand and to provide more granular control over who can enable, manage, and use AI capabilities, including a new who can manage option that replaces the existing Allow Copilot and Facilitator meeting option:

  • Who can manage AI - replaces the existing Allow Copilot and Facilitator option and determines who can turn Copilot and other AI features on or off during a meeting. If an admin turns Meeting AI off, this option is set to No one.
  • Who can use AI - provides more granular control over which meeting participants can use Copilot and other AI capabilities.
  • Start Transcription with AI - lets organizers choose whether transcription starts with AI. Administrators can also control this option through Teams admin center.
  • Intelligent Recap controls - lets organizers decide whether an Intelligent Recap is created when Copilot is turned on, including for meetings where a transcript is not created.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Targeted Release (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 and expect to complete by early December 2026.

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late November 2026 and expect to complete by early December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Today, the Copilot policy combines whether AI is available in a meeting with whether a saved transcript is required. After this update, these behaviors are represented by two separate settings:

  • Allow AI in meetings: On / Off, but organizers can change / Off, and organizers cannot change
  • Start transcription when AI is turned on: On, but organizers can change / On, and organizers cannot change / Off

To keep the experience predictable and avoid invalid combinations: if MeetingAI is set to enforced off, transcription will also be turned off; if transcription is then turned back on, MeetingAI will no longer be enforced off.

In PowerShell, administrators will use MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI instead of the existing Copilot policy. Once the new controls are enabled, the Copilot policy can no longer be updated directly - attempts will return guidance to use the new policies.

What happens to existing configurations: Microsoft will perform a one-time update mapping each existing Copilot value to the corresponding MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI values, preserving the current effective behavior for your organization. Administrators do not need to recreate their policies. Examples include:

Copilot is on and uses a saved transcript by defaultOnOn, but organizers can change
Copilot is on and a saved transcript is requiredOnOn, and organizers cannot change
Copilot is available without transcriptionOnOff
Copilot is off, but organizers can enable itOff, but organizers can changeBased on the existing transcription configuration
Copilot is enforced offOff, and organizers cannot changeOff
Existing configurationMeetingAITranscriptionWithMeetingAI

The Transcription policy remains available and continues to control whether transcription is allowed. The new TranscriptionWithMeetingAI policy controls whether transcription starts when meeting AI is turned on.

The new settings will appear in the Teams admin center meeting policy under Recording and transcription and Copilot and other AI.

[Insert provided Teams admin center screenshot here]

The screenshot shows the new Start transcription when AI is turned on control and Allow AI in all meetings control, including the options administrators can use to set defaults or prevent organizers from changing the configured behavior.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required to migrate existing configurations. Before rollout, we recommend admins:

  • Review any automation or scripts that read or update the Copilot meeting policy, and update them to use MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI.
  • Review custom tooling, runbooks, or documentation referencing the Copilot policy.
  • Inform Teams administrators that existing behavior will now be represented by two settings in Teams admin center.
  • Confirm the mapped configuration reflects intended behavior once the new controls are available.

If you do not use PowerShell or custom automation to manage Teams meeting policies, no action is required. Existing configurations will be mapped automatically.

[Compliance considerations:]

This change affects administrative controls over AI and transcription availability in meetings but does not alter how existing customer data is processed or stored. Review AI and transcription governance policies for your organization as appropriate.

Updated October 30, 2026: We have updated this post with additional information as the feature is now generally available. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT) is now generally available in Microsoft Entra ID. With CYOT, your organization can deliver SMS and voice authentication through a supported telecom provider of its choice. You purchase the provider's offer in Microsoft Security Store and manage the commercial relationship directly with the provider. 

Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication begins retiring on February 1, 2027. To keep SMS and voice authentication available for users who need it, set up CYOT before that date. 

Microsoft recommends phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys, instead of SMS or voice. Use telephony-based authentication only for users who have a business, regulatory, or technical need for it.

[What you need to do]

If your organization plans to use CYOT: 

  1. Identify users who need SMS or voice. Confirm which users have a requirement that phishing-resistant methods can't meet. 
  2. Choose a provider. Compare the supported telecom providers on coverage, channels, pricing, support, and compliance. 
  3. Check purchasing requirements. Confirm that you have a paid Azure subscription that is eligible for Security Store purchases, and that you have the Owner role, or Contributor plus Role Based Access Control Administrator.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Meeting memory file generation
item.description:
Updated October 30, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why]

Microsoft Teams is introducing AI generated meeting memory files that capture key insights from meetings (formerly archive files). These files help Microsoft 365 Copilot and Facilitator deliver more accurate context aware responses while maintaining strong privacy controls by not storing raw meeting content. This capability supports enterprise ready AI by improving knowledge grounding while keeping data secure and manageable.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 558933.

[Rollout Schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning early January 2027 (previously early November 2026) and expected to complete mid-January 2027 (previously mid-November 2026)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning mid-January 2027 (previously early December 2026) and expected to complete late January 2027 (previously early January)

Teams admin center controls for this feature will be available approximately four weeks before memory file generation begins. The dates above reflect when admin controls become available.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Teams administrators
  • Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot or Facilitator capabilities enabled

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • SharePoint Embedded

What will happen

  • AI meeting memory files (.meeting files) will be generated for meetings where Intelligent Recap is turned on. The feature is enabled by default in your organization.
  • Memory files are stored in a tenant-owned SharePoint Embedded container, not in user storage. You can control the default expiration time for these files within your organization.
  • Users cannot directly view or access memory files.
  • When the feature is released, Facilitator will use the memory to answer questions about meetings and responses include citations linking to meeting recaps or invites. In the future, Copilot will also use the memory to answer questions about meetings. 
  • Memory files cannot be modified, renamed, or moved.
  • All content in memory files is AI-generated. No raw transcript snippets are stored.
  • Memory generation requires all of the following:
    • Meeting memory is enabled for your organization.
    • Intelligent Recap is enabled for the meeting.
  • Memory files are not created for:
    • Meetings with sensitivity labels that include encryption
    • End-to-end encrypted meetings
    • Meetings with restricted copying or forwarding
  • Access and data protection:
    • Only users with access to the meeting can receive responses grounded in its memory and AI tools do not surface insights to users who do not have meeting access.
    • Memory knowledge is only shared with users who are in the same tenant as the meeting organizer.

[Action Required / Recommendations]

No immediate action is required. However, administrators should review configuration settings and consider organizational policy alignment.

Admins can enable or disable this feature in the Teams admin center.

Recommended actions:

  • Review the AI archive setting in Teams admin center before rollout. Setting path: Meeting Policies > Meeting Memory".
  • Evaluate the default expiration period, which is set to five years (1,825 days), and adjust retention settings as needed to align with compliance policies.
  • Communicate this capability to helpdesk teams and compliance stakeholders.
  • Monitor availability of the memory setting in Teams admin center and review or update settings when they become available. Memory file generation will begin 4 weeks after the setting is released to your organization.

Learn more: AI Archives for Microsoft Teams Meetings | Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn 

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data, and if so, where, and is the data cached or permanently stored?Yes. The change introduces AI-generated meeting memory files that are stored in a tenant-owned SharePoint Embedded container and retained according to a configurable retention period.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Meeting transcripts and metadata are processed into structured AI memory files that enable downstream AI systems such as Copilot and Facilitator to reason over meeting content.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI or machine learning capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Copilot and Facilitator use AI meeting memory files to generate context-aware responses grounded in prior meeting content.
Does the change provide users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with Copilot and Facilitator, which leverage meeting memory  data to answer questions and provide insights about meetings.
Does the change modify retention policies, holds, or deletion workflows?Yes. AI meeting memory files are governed by a default retention period of five years and are automatically deleted upon expiration.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Administrators can enable or disable AI meeting memory generation and configure retention settings in the Teams Admin Center.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Migrate Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing before EWS deprecation
item.description:
Updated October 30, 2026: Gov rollout of this feature is paused at this time. We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for any inconvenience.

[What and Why:]

Exchange Web Services (EWS) deprecation begins October 1, 2026. Cross-tenant collaboration features — Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing — currently rely on EWS.

Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips will be available by September 2026 and Calendar Sharing will be available by early November 2026 (previously end-October) via Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy, which replaces EWS-based cross-tenant collaboration.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in August 2026 and expect to complete by September 15, 2026 for Free/Busy, Mailtips and November 6, 2026 (previously October 30) for Calendar Sharing.
  • GCC, GCC High, DoD: We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

[Impact on your organization:]

Sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips (e.g., out of office message) with another Microsoft 365 organization via Organization Relationship or Sharing Policy relies on Exchange Web Services (EWS), which is being deprecated. To preserve these cross-tenant collaboration scenarios, you will need to start migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policy.

Your tenant is affected if it uses any of the following Exchange Online configurations:

  • Organization Relationships — sharing Free/Busy or MailTips with other Microsoft 365 tenants 
  • Sharing Policies — sharing calendars externally, either via invitations sent to recipients in other Microsoft 365 organizations or calendars published for anonymous access via an internet URL

Run these commands in Exchange Online PowerShell to check if your tenant is affected: 

    • Get-OrganizationRelationship | Format-List Name, DomainNames, Enabled, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel, FreeBusyAccessScope, MailTipsAccessEnabled, MailTipsAccessLevel, MailTipsAccessScopeIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) either FreeBusyAccessEnabled: True or MailtipsAccessEnabled: True, and (3) the external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed. 
    • Get-SharingPolicy | Format-List Name, Domains, Enabled, DefaultIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) the Domains property contains at least one rule with a CalendarSharingFreeBusy access level (Simple, Detail, or Reviewer), and (3) the targeted external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, and (4) the policy is assigned to one or more mailboxes, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed.
    • Note: rules that begin with Anonymous: represent calendar publishing to anonymous internet recipients via a published URL - these also appear in this output.

What happens if I do nothing:

Starting October 1, 2026, Exchange Web Services (EWS) will be gradually disabled in line with previous communications linked to this message. As this rollout reaches your tenant, cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing that rely on EWS will be affected — recipients in partner organizations may no longer see Free/Busy, MailTips, or shared calendars from your tenant. 

If your organization is not ready to migrate, you can retain EWS access by following the guidance of the latest blog we published: ExchangeOnline EWS, Your Time is Almost Up (EWSEnabled set to True) while you prepare and execute the migration steps attached to this message. EWS access through this extension will remain available until the final EWS shutdown on April 1, 2027. 

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Follow this Message center post for updates to the rollout schedule. To avoid impact, plan to migrate after the rollout reaches your tenant and before EWS deprecation.
  • Review the migration guide linked below for step-by-step instructions to understand your current configurations, set up new Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policies, validate the new configurations, and remove unused configurations. 
  • Check the blog post linked below for additional information and answers to frequently asked questions. 
  • Hybrid and on-premises scenarios are not in scope. This update applies to fully cloud-hosted (Exchange Online ↔ Exchange Online) cross-tenant and cross-cloud configurations only. For organizations running on-premises Exchange and Exchange Online in a Hybrid Deployment, migrate to Dedicated Hybrid App. For organizations hosted in Exchange Online sharing with another organization running Exchange on-premises, kindly monitor future Message Center posts for guidance on migration paths as they become available. 

[Additional information:]

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams: Threads will become the default layout for new channels created with Microsoft Graph

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Explicit consent for PSTN participants in one-to-one calls

  • This capability uses the existing explicit consent setting in Teams calling policies. It does not introduce a new admin policy setting.

[Action required and recommendations]

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Authenticator: Usability improvements for iOS and Android
item.description:
Updated October 29, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We’re updating Microsoft Authenticator with several usability improvements across iOS and Android. These updates include a refreshed home experience, clearer guidance for accounts that need to be restored, improvements to restoration and sign-in flows, and additional prompts designed to help keep Authenticator working reliably. Availability and timing vary by platform.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD): Beginning in early November 2026 (previously October) and expected to complete in late November 2026
  • The improved restoration experience for push notifications and passwordless sign-in will be available on iOS first, with Android planned to follow in January 2027.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users of Microsoft Authenticator on iOS and Android

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Authenticator for iOS and Android

What will happen

  • Improved Authenticator home experience, iOS and Android: The Authenticator home page is being updated to improve the experience when users view and manage their accounts. On Android, this update will be available in November 2026.

iOs:

Android:

  • Clearer notification for accounts that haven’t been restored, iOS and Android: Users with accounts that have not yet been restored will see a banner informing them that those accounts require attention

. 

  • Improved first-run guidance for account restoration, iOS and Android: The first-run experience will more clearly show which accounts need to be restored, giving users additional context during Authenticator setup.

  • App rating prompt during sign-in, iOS only: Users may see an option to rate Microsoft Authenticator as part of the sign-in experience, giving them an opportunity to provide feedback about the app. 
  • Improved restoration experience for push notifications and passwordless sign-in: The restoration flow is being improved for users who use push notifications and passwordless sign-in. This improvement will be available on iOS first, with Android planned for January 2027. 
  • Prompt to exclude Authenticator from battery optimization, Android only: After successfully completing an interactive authentication, users may see a non-blocking prompt to exclude Authenticator from Android battery optimization. Excluding the app from battery optimization helps users stay signed in and continue receiving work or school notifications. The prompt will not block authentication.

[Action required and recommendations]

No configuration action is specified in this request.

  • Inform your help desk and security operations teams about the updated Authenticator experiences.
  • Update internal user guidance and screenshots that show the previous Authenticator experiences.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Initiate side conversations within the meeting chat window
item.description:
Updated October 29, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Microsoft Teams will enable meeting participants to start and continue one-to-one or small-group conversations directly from the meeting chat experience. Users can create a side conversation without leaving the meeting context, helping them coordinate, ask questions, share information, and collaborate in parallel while keeping the main meeting discussion focused.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out in early December 2026 (previously early January 2027) and expect to complete in mid-January 2027 (previously late January).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users will be able to start or continue private 1:1 and group chats directly from the meeting chat experience, without leaving the meeting window. Existing chat history is preserved, so conversations remain part of the user’s regular Teams chat history.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required. This feature does not introduce a new chat surface, admin policy, or meeting option. Users can turn off the side-chat tab experience if they prefer not to use it.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
